transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’m here because I keep messing up basic things. Like paying bills, replying to interview emails, going to appointments, running errands. I forget or don’t follow through, and it’s starting to actually cost me opportunities.
Are these mistakes and forgetfulness affecting your daily life or relationships in any significant way?

Yeah… it is. Since I got fired, I’ve missed follow-ups for interviews, and I had to step back from a volunteer project I actually cared about. So I’m just… unemployed, and it feels like I can’t reliably manage the basic steps to move forward.
Do you often find yourself doing more activities or taking on more tasks than you can handle?

Yeah… I think so. Even now, without a job, I’m kind of moving from one thing to another all day. Laundry, emails, opening and reorganizing tabs, pacing around, starting dinner… but a lot of it doesn’t actually get finished. It’s like I can’t really let myself stop.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?

Yeah… mostly in conversations. I’ll answer before someone’s even finished asking, because I think I know what they mean. Then I realize I cut them off, or I answered a different question than they were asking. It’s embarrassing.
Do you feel overwhelmed or anxious when you think about your current situation and all the tasks you're trying to manage?
I’m not really sure. I mean… I don’t think of it as anxiety exactly. It’s more like I just look at everything and kind of shut down. Then I avoid it for a while.
Do you often feel guilty or criticize yourself for your mistakes or inability to follow through on tasks?
I don’t know… probably sometimes. I don’t really think about it that directly. I just get frustrated with myself when things don’t get done, I guess.
Do you often feel a physical need to be moving or doing something?

Yeah… pretty often. If I’m sitting through an interview or a meeting, or even just a movie, I get this… pressure, I guess, like I need to move or do something with my hands. Otherwise I feel really uncomfortable, like I can’t stay still.
Do you feel upset or emotional when you're unable to complete tasks or follow through on things?

Yeah… I mean, I do get upset, but mostly because it just keeps happening. Like if someone gives me steps for a job application or something around the apartment, I’ll start out okay, and then somehow it turns into half-finished forms, emails I never sent, or piles of stuff I moved but didn’t actually put away. It’s… frustrating.
Do you often find yourself getting easily irritated or angry when things don't go as planned?
I’m not really sure. I mean… I can get annoyed when things change or don’t work out, but I don’t know if I’d call it angry exactly. It kind of depends.
Do you often find yourself having trouble focusing on one task for a long period of time?

Yeah. I’ll sit down to do one thing, like update my resume or work on a coding problem, and then… a text pops up, or I hear someone outside, or I just think of some other thing I should do, and I’m off track before I really notice.
Do you experience these problems with following through on tasks and paying attention at home, at work, or in social situations?

Yeah… mostly with work-type stuff, I guess. Since I got fired, I’ve missed follow-ups after interviews, and I had to step back from a volunteer project I actually cared about. So it’s been affecting things pretty badly. I’m not really managing the basic steps to move forward right now.
Do you have trouble following through on tasks or paying attention in social situations with friends or family?

Yeah… I think so. If someone gives me steps to follow, like for an application or a volunteer thing, I’ll start out okay, but then it kind of falls apart. I’ll end up with forms half done, emails I meant to send, or stuff around the apartment that I moved but didn’t actually put away.
Have you had trouble with following through on tasks and paying attention for as long as you can remember?

Yeah… I think so. I remember even in elementary school, teachers would say I was bright, but I’d lose worksheets all the time, rush through directions, talk when I wasn’t supposed to, and my desk was always such a mess I couldn’t find assignments. So… it’s kind of always been there.
Do you have intense mood swings, where your emotions shift quickly?
I’m not really sure. I mean… I get frustrated or overwhelmed sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed intense mood swings like that.
Do you often fidget with your hands or feet when you're sitting still?

Yeah. I don’t always notice it, but if I’m sitting through something like an interview or a movie, I feel like I need to shift around or do something with my hands. It’s kind of like… this pressure, like I can’t just sit still.
Did you have a lot of energy and difficulty sitting still when you were a child?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, teachers wrote stuff like I was bright, but I’d talk out of turn, rush through directions, lose worksheets, and my desk was always so messy I couldn’t find things. So sitting still and staying settled was… not really easy for me.
Do you often have strong emotional reactions to small setbacks or disappointments?
I don’t really know. I mean, I can get upset if something goes wrong, but I’m not sure if it’s stronger than normal. I haven’t really paid attention to it that way.
Do you have trouble managing your emotions when faced with stressful or frustrating situations?
I’m not really sure. Stress definitely makes me feel tense, but I don’t know if I’d say I have trouble managing my emotions. I kind of just… deal with it, I guess.
Do you often interrupt others or blurt out answers before they've finished speaking?
Yeah… I do that. I’ll think I know what someone’s about to ask or say, and I jump in before they’re finished. Then sometimes I realize I answered the wrong thing or that I kind of cut them off.
Have you experienced these difficulties with following through on tasks, paying attention, and impulsivity for as long as you can remember, even as a child?

Yeah… I think so. I remember in elementary school teachers would say I was bright, but I was always losing worksheets or not following directions right because I rushed. I talked out of turn a lot, too. My desk was usually such a mess I couldn’t find my assignments.
